background_notes.fact: For gamma>0 and real mean-zero g in H^gamma with norm at most R, g_m=P_{<=m}g is a smooth real mean-zero trigonometric polynomial, ||g_m||_{H^gamma}<=R, ||g_m||_2+||g||_2<=2R, and ||g_m-g||_2 tends to zero as m tends to infinity.

grounds.reason: Sobolev norm is the weighted Fourier square sum; reality and zero mean are specified in Fourier coefficients.
The arbitrary g belongs to the stated ball and is real and mean-zero.
The cutoff is explicitly the multiplier 1_{|k|<=m}.

background_notes.justification: A finite Fourier sum is smooth. The symmetric real cutoff preserves conjugate symmetry and the zero coefficient. Deleting terms contracts the nonnegative weighted square sum. Since <k>^(2 gamma)>=1, both L2 norms are at most R. The omitted unweighted square sum is bounded by the tail of the convergent weighted square sum and hence tends to zero. These facts also check the B0=2R premise in the N001 application.

background_notes.fact: P is a contraction on each H^s; Dinv and Dinv2 are bounded on each H^s with norm at most 1 and annihilate the zero mode. Dinv:L2->H^1 has norm at most sqrt(2), also for inputs of nonzero mean. P,Dinv,Dinv2 preserve reality. Consequently all occurrences of these multipliers in D009-D010 act continuously on their displayed H^1 or L2 inputs.

grounds.reason: The norms and reality condition are specified Fourierwise.
P0 retains only the zero mode.
Dinv has multiplier 1/(ik) for nonzero k and zero at k=0.
Dinv2 is the composition of Dinv with itself.

background_notes.justification: In the Fourier norm the multiplier of P has modulus at most 1, and on nonzero integer modes |1/k| and |1/k^2| are at most 1. For the gain from L2 to H^1, (1+k^2)/k^2<=2 at k!=0. Thus the asserted bounds follow termwise from the norm sums; zero modes are removed. Each multiplier satisfies m(-k)=conjugate(m(k)), so it preserves the reality condition. Equivalently Dinv f=Dinv(Pf), checking the general-L2 use of the mean-zero N006 estimate.

background_notes.fact: On the normalized torus, (f,h)->P0(fh) is a continuous bilinear scalar map on L2 x L2, with |P0(fh)|<=||f||_2||h||_2 and |P0(f^2)-P0(h^2)|<=(||f||_2+||h||_2)||f-h||_2. A bilinear product satisfying the N006 H^1 algebra estimate is continuous on H^1 x H^1; its finite powers and finite compositions with the supplied bounded linear maps are continuous. Hence each term in D009-D010 is continuous from L2 into H^1 for fixed tau>0.

grounds.reason: The integration measure is dx/(2 pi).
L2 has the normalized Fourier/L2 convention.
P0 is the spatial mean, agreeing with the zero Fourier coefficient.
H^1 product norm is bounded by C times the product of the norms, and S_t is a Sobolev isometry.
F_tau uses squares of inverse derivatives and bounded projections/Airy maps.
The four H_tau terms consist of these products, scalar means and inverse derivatives, with finite coefficients at positive fixed tau.

background_notes.justification: The integral Cauchy-Schwarz inequality applied to |f|,|h| bounds the mean of fh; applying it to (f-h)(f+h) proves the square-difference bound. For H^1 products use ab-cd=(a-c)b+c(b-d) and the given algebra estimate; convergent sequences are bounded, so products converge. Iterating this argument handles cubes and mixed products. BG002 gives the bounded inverse-derivative maps. In the first H_tau term both factors lie in H^1; the second is an H^1 function times the continuous scalar mean; the third is an H^1 cube followed by Dinv; the fourth is a product of two H^1 factors followed by Dinv2. S_t and P preserve H^1, and the finitely many scalar coefficients cause no issue for fixed tau.

background_notes.fact: For a fixed finite grid, if x_{m,n}->x_n and y_{m,n}->y_n in L2 for every grid index n, and ||x_{m,n}-y_{m,n}||_2<=K for all m,n with K independent of m,n, then max_n||x_n-y_n||_2<=K.

grounds.reason: F001 provides exact-flow convergence and the common smooth-grid bound K=C0 tau^gamma.
F002 provides iterate convergence on every fixed finite grid.
L and tau=T/L are fixed before taking the approximation limit, and 0<=n<=L.

background_notes.justification: The triangle inequality yields | ||x_{m,n}-y_{m,n}||_2-||x_n-y_n||_2 |<=||x_{m,n}-x_n||_2+||y_{m,n}-y_n||_2, which tends to zero for each n. Passing to the limit gives the bound K for each of the finitely many indices; taking their finite maximum retains K. No uniformity in the number of grid points or in tau is required for this limit.
